A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RaCO-DP research, with matching core algorithms, theoretical results and appendices A-F. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison despite reformatting and relocated plots.

before.justification: V1 reports original RaCO-DP experiments on fairness and false-negative-rate constraints, computational timings, and clipping and constraint-update analyses in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds CelebA neural-network experiments, equalized-odds evaluations and low-privacy-budget analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 3-4 retain the same generalized constraints, private histogram, clipped primal gradients and post-processed dual updates. ResNet16 is an additional evaluation model using the existing framework; no new RaCO-DP algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: V2 adds image-based demographic-parity evaluation on CelebA and equalized-odds evaluation on Credit-Card. Equalized odds was already defined in v1's Appendix A but was not empirically evaluated. The original Adult, Credit-Card, Parkinsons, ACSEmployment and Heart coverage remains.

E2.justification: Clearly identifiable comparisons retain SGDA, DP-FERMI and Tran et al.; the new experiments reuse SGDA or DP-FERMI. Both versions also name Jagielski et al., but v2 Figure 4 adds Jagielski legend entries without a clearly distinguishable additional plotted series. The PDFs therefore do not reliably establish whether actual comparator participation changed.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a 6.4-million-parameter ResNet16 evaluation configuration and expands privacy sweeps: several tabular comparisons gain epsilon=0.5, ACSEmployment gains epsilon=1 and 3, and Adult gains epsilon=0.01 and 0.1. These are additional experimental settings; changed splits are not established. Figure 4 and Appendix E.3 inconsistently list epsilon=2 where the plotted panels show 3.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.8 and Figure 9 examine how very small privacy budgets affect Adult accuracy, fairness and variability. The clipping-norm and hard-versus-soft constraint analyses are retained: v1 Figures 6-7 become v2 Figure 8.

E5.justification: V1 already reports five-seed tuning, 20 final models, plot uncertainty bands and timing variability. V2 explicitly discusses 95% confidence intervals in the low-epsilon analysis and specifies five-seed averaging for CelebA, without detailing confidence-interval construction. The retained tabular run counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds CelebA results, including approximately 90% accuracy at epsilon=1 and target gamma=0.1 versus approximately 95% for non-private SGDA, plus Credit-Card equalized-odds and low-epsilon Adult results. Privacy-sweep entries expand, and the Heart FNR and ACSEmployment frontiers are revised or extended. Table 2's timing values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 and the mathematical definitions, lemmas and proofs in Appendices A-D are retained, including the existing equalized-odds formulation. Expanded dataset notation in Definition 2.1 and citation or formatting edits do not substantively change the theory.

C1.justification: The general rate-constrained DP framework, histogram privacy-cost claim and convergence contribution remain. V2's abstract and introduction add an empirical claim of practical neural-network scalability. The introduction also removes v1's parenthetical identification of approximate stationarity with a local optimum.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains near-non-private accuracy through favorable sample-size-to-dimension ratios and rapid convergence, while noting a wider gap for ResNet16. Appendix E.8 interprets deterioration under very small privacy budgets. V2 removes the explicit caveat that hyperparameter-tuning privacy loss is excluded; the clipping and soft-dual-update limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability link and neural-network implementation details, including 16-group normalization, batch size 256, learning rates and noise settings. It removes v1's 75/25 train-test split, 15% validation reservation and explanation of privacy-limited training-step selection. Existing tabular tuning and CPU benchmark details largely remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds the ResNet and CelebA references and removes Papernot and Steinke's hyperparameter-tuning reference. Section 7 drops v1's characterization of Lowy et al.'s Lipschitz assumption and emphasizes direct constraint optimization versus a proxy objective. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and several technical passages receive wording edits, and Section 6 is reorganized around setup, tabular results, neural networks, scaling and interpretation. Citation style, author/publication metadata and appendix headings change, while the overall section sequence and most methodological and proof exposition remain.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially reorganizes the experimental displays. Figure 2 now features CelebA, Parkinsons and ACSEmployment; Adult curves move into expanded Figure 4; equalized-odds and low-epsilon plots are added; and v1 Figures 6-7 are merged into Figure 8. Panel arrangements, axes, legends and captions change extensively.

improvement.justification: The neural-network and equalized-odds evaluations strengthen empirical support for applicability beyond v1's logistic-regression experiments, while the privacy-gap explanation and low-epsilon analysis better qualify practical performance. The code pointer and neural-training details also help reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by lost split and accounting disclosures, especially the omitted hyperparameter-tuning privacy-loss caveat, and inconsistent or ambiguous plot labels.
